subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a militarized futuristic truck design with an armored cab, missile turret on the cargo bed, neon strips, antenna, and light bar, deciding to keep the model static without wheel joints for simplicity.

Working out dimensions and layout: an 8m long, 3m wide, 3.2m tall body with three wheel axles, low-poly cylinder wheels with glowing hubs, flat-colored metal panels using the clockwork kit, and a chassis frame positioned with wheels sized to clear the ground properly.

Now I'm defining the hull shape with an extruded wedge profile along the z/y plane, sketching out the front hood sloping down and the cab body's angular outline point by point.

Working out the windshield slab's position and tilt angle, I'm computing the box dimensions and rotation needed so its normal faces up and forward correctly, settling on a -45° rotation about the X axis.

I'm planning the windshield texture as a dark teal gradient with cyan scanline hex accents mapped onto an angled plane, then laying out side windows as trapezoid-textured planes on the cab's side faces.

For wheel positioning I'm checking that the wheels sit slightly inset into the body profile, then adding angular box-shaped fenders above each wheel for an armored look, plus mudguards. For the cargo section, I'm blocking out the chassis extending behind the cab and starting to shape an armored cargo module as an extruded profile.

Now I'm planning a flat deck platform with a rotating turret, side armor panels, an angled missile pod rack, a rail gun turret on a ring mount, plus a rear ramp, lights, fuel drums, and an antenna mast. Writing helper functions for boxes and cylinders...

Still writing helpers...

For textures and surface detail, I'm thinking through a glass windshield, side windows, hazard stripe decals, a stylized emblem/sigil for the doors, and a custom camo paint scheme using dark navy, charcoal, and teal patches across the panelled hull.

I'm also planning extras like a glowing neon "2077" sign, a radar/HUD screen texture for the turret, a warning label plate, slit-style glowing headlights, and a tire tread approach that distinguishes sidewall from tread using lug patterns based on the cylinder's angular coordinate.

Now I'm thinking through the lighting approach: applying a glow effect to neon strips along the sides in cyan and magenta, plus a thin magenta underglow strip beneath the chassis, while keeping the part count manageable around 200 for efficient output. I'm settling on a cyberpunk palette of dark gunmetal and near-black hull tones accented by bright cyan and magenta neon colors rather than olive camo.

Setting up the imports and build structure, pulling in metal and panelled kits while deciding to skip the gear train and decorative cog emblem to keep things simpler.

For the cab extrusion, I'm sorting out the extrude orientation and applying a panelled camo paint with specific panel sizing and rivet spacing, then checking texture resolution density against the model's surface area.

Realizing the seam lines at 2.5mm would be mostly subpixel even at higher paint resolutions, so I decide to write a custom "plated" paint function instead, defining seam width and grid size parameters to control panel line visibility directly.

Writing seam detection logic...

Now I'm planning additional surface details: blending in a top-down sky tint based on surface normal, adding camo-style patches, and checking which paint utility functions are available for resolving colors, mixing, and noise. Then I shift to laying out the wheel positions, figuring a six-wheel configuration with front and rear axle placements, wheel radius, and spacing to fit a reasonable wheelbase.

Working through geometry to avoid clipping -- adjusting body half-width and wheel center positioning so the fenders properly clear the wheel tops without overlap. Still defining wheel construction...

Still positioning the truck body...

Maybe I'll restrict the hazard paint to just the bottom band instead of the whole ram surface. Now I'm placing glowing headlight slits on the nose, checking that their position at y 1.65 doesn't collide with the ram's overlapping geometry near the top edges.

Working out hood slat placement...

Adding roof equipment next...

Setting the dish's lathe axis so it opens upward toward +y. Now I'm positioning side mirrors, door emblems, and window panels on the cab—placing decal planes at specific coordinates on the sides for doors, emblems, and windshield geometry.

I need to make sure the window plane stays within the side silhouette boundary, since the windshield slants back at the top. I'll shape it as a trapezoid in the texture, keeping the bottom full width but cutting the top on a slant so it doesn't poke outside the cab's profile.

Now I'm working out orientation: for the plane facing +x (left side, viewed from outside looking toward -x), the viewer's right points toward -z, which means the truck's front ends up on the left side of the drawing for that face.

To avoid needing mirrored textures, I'm opting for a symmetric window shape that cuts both top corners rather than just one, so a single texture works for both sides. Now I'm sizing the windshield relative to the cab width.

Positioning the windshield at the 45° frame angle, offsetting it slightly outward along the surface normal, and deciding to skip wipers and pillars for simplicity. Then I'm moving to the cargo section behind the cab, setting up the deck frame dimensions and starting on armored sidewalls for a weapons bay.

For the sidewalls, I'm switching to extruded "ammo locker" shapes with a stepped angular profile along the side, mirrored on both sides of the vehicle with a central gap reserved for the turret, plus a rear-end box to close off the deck.

Still working out locker proportions and surface details like vent slats, neon strip accents, hatch handles, and label plates. I'm now sketching the turret itself—a layered base ring, a hexagonal body, and a side-extruded head profile—sitting centered on the deck bay.

I realize the barrels pointing forward would collide with the cab roof height, so I need to either raise the turret higher or mount it on an elevated pedestal to clear the cab geometry.

Settling on: pedestal at y 2.9, turret head center around y 3.35, barrels at y 3.4 — that clears both the roof and the lockers at 2.9, giving a total height near 4m, which is exaggerated compared to real military trucks but fits the cyberpunk aesthetic.

Now I'm adding angled missile pods on both lockers with glowing red tube openings and orange cone-shaped rocket tips, plus rear details like glowing tail lights, a ramp, tow hitch, and a sensor mast antenna array near the back.

Overall vehicle length checks out around 8.6 meters nose to tail, which feels right. I'm also placing side-mounted energy cell tanks between the front and rear axle wheel wells, fitting them into the gap along the body.

Now I'm adding a glowing magenta underbody rod running lengthwise, plus small exhaust stacks positioned behind the cab near the body sides.

Exhaust stacks get clamp bands and glowing orange tips. For the cab, I'm detailing door handles, step plates, grab handles, fuel hatch, headlamp cages, bull bar, and roof spotlights, plus a dark slatted grille between the headlights glowing cyan from behind.

I'm building a reusable studs helper that merges box/sphere geometries for rivet rows, then using it to add cheap ERA-style armor tiles across the locker and cab side surfaces.

Now I'm defining the camo paint pattern using patches with a dark base and mottled grays, plus a plated() helper for seam lines, and weighing whether a static rig is sufficient without a full joint setup.

For the wheels, I'm checking the geometry so the 12-sided cylinder actually touches the floor — balancing vertex versus flat-face orientation to decide on a center height of 0.70 and radius 0.74, keeping the sink within an acceptable 2% tolerance.

Now I'm moving on to the SVG textures: designing a windshield with a dark gradient, cyan HUD lines and diagonal reflection stripes within slanted rounded corners, a hexagonal side window with dark fill and reflection highlights, and a circular emblem with a magenta ring.

I'm sketching more textures too: a bold "77" hexagon emblem with chevrons, a health/cell bar panel with glowing cyan-to-lime gradient bars on a dark background, a neon "2077" rear sign with magenta text and a cyan underline glow, and considering a turret sight decal with a red lens "eye."

I'm also planning a stenciled plate reading "UNIT 07 // ARC-WOLF" on the outer locker face, done as pale yellow cut-out text with a transparent background and no glow, positioned on the locker's outward-facing plane and oriented so it reads correctly from the viewer's side.

Now I'm laying out the ERA tiles lower on the locker (around y 1.7–2.3 in three rows) so they don't collide with the nameplate above at y~2.62, and adding fender boxes over each wheel position.

I'm also adding mudflaps behind the rear wheels, differential housing spheres at each axle, and a driveshaft rod running along the chassis centerline between the front and rear axles.

For the cab, I'm fixing the nose profile dimensions and placing roof details: a sensor turret ball with a lens glow, a tilted satellite dish, and antennas at the rear roof corners with small red glowing tips.

Now I'm adding side mirrors with angled arm rods and mirror boxes with tiny camera-lens glows, plus door seam details using thin vertical and horizontal strips to mark panel lines and the beltline.

I'm also placing a running board box along each side and checking its position against the fuel tank boxes so they don't collide, adjusting tank width and z-length to fit cleanly between the wheels.

Now I'm adding neon accent strips—thin glowing boxes along the cab beltline, locker edges, and hood centerline in magenta and cyan—then moving on to turret details, starting with a plated cylindrical pedestal built at the turret's z position.

Still defining turret geometry...

Planning the dual cannon barrels with muzzle brakes, heat sleeves, and recoil housings, then skipping ERA tiles and placing a glowing reticle "eye" box on the turret's sloped front face.

Positioning the reticle off-center with barrels symmetric at ±.28, keeping plane width within bounds. Checking total turret height with antennas and mast clearance, then working out missile pod placement on the lockers, tilting each pod box forward along a rotated axis so the front face angles upward correctly.

For the tube layout on each pod's front face, I'll compute a quaternion from the pod's -25° rotation and apply it to local offsets to get world positions for a 2x3 grid of cylindrical tubes, then add small conical rocket tips just beyond each tube opening.

Now I'm checking placement conflicts: side pods sit around x ±.95 with lockers extending from x 0.7 to 1.2, clear of the turret barrels at ±.28, with a cradle box supporting each pod from below. For the rear, I'm adding a bumper box, glowing red tail lights, and making sure the rear pan and lockers line up with the deck frame's z-extent.

Positioning the rear bumper and checking wheel clearance at the back. For the rear bay between the pedestal and bumper, I'm considering adding a couple of cargo crates around z -3.3, maybe painted orange for a hazard look.

I'm also sketching a glowing drone landing pad for the deck—a circular "H" marker—plus a tiny quad drone made from a small box body with four rotor discs, sized to sit on the pad. With the part count growing, I'm ready to start writing the actual code, aiming to keep it around 450 lines.

I'm setting up the builder helper functions: box, cylinder, glow, and plane utilities that wrap the geometry creation with position, rotation, and texture options, making sure optional rotation/direction parameters don't break things.

Now I'm handling merging stud geometries using BufferGeometryUtils, limiting the flat color palette to around 25 to stay efficient, and sketching out a "plated" paint pattern function using fractional coordinates.

Writing shading logic...

Still defining paint functions...

Still writing axle geometry...

Adding bolt positions...

Now I'm skipping brake calipers for simplicity and planning the full part layout: ten pieces per wheel across sixty total wheel parts, plus hull panels and paint colors for the cab extrusion. I'm also sketching the windshield frame with A-pillar rods running from the lower cab corners up to the roofline.

I'm adding a roof visor as a small overlapping box above the front window, then planning bull bar spikes as cones mounted on the ram, angled slightly forward across three positions.

Now I'm detailing the spike helper with direction and length parameters, picking a steel-grey hazard color, and reminding myself to prefix unused variables with underscores to avoid typecheck issues before writing the final code, including the merged armor tile geometry loop.

Still writing tile geometry...

I'll skip rivets and extra decorative details to keep things manageable, and focus on adding an antenna with a glowing red tip, a rear mast with a cross dish plate, and start sketching the drone body—keeping the overall build under 40 lines.

Placing exhaust stacks near the lockers with heat shields and glowing band rings, plus a drone pad setup—I think I have enough now to write the full build.
